title: 一个人长期失权，就会讨厌社交 | 原文
content: Chronic disempowerment in social interactions leads people to avoid communication. Individuals who lack control in conversations—unable to set boundaries, choose topics, or end encounters at will—experience socializing as exhausting rather than enjoyable. This is distinct from introversion or social anxiety. The article identifies four signs of social disempowerment: preferring online to phone communication, declining invitations, lurking in group chats, and needing recovery time after events. People may develop this pattern through childhood experiences of being ignored, criticized, or forced into compliance during interactions. The core issue is not disliking people but lacking autonomy in how engagement occurs.
